name: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention
problem: Linear attention could not be scaled to hundreds of billions of parameters in practice, because long-context training of linear attention requires computation-communication overlap techniques nobody had made efficient.
mechanism: Scales lightning attention (Lightning Attention-2's causal tiling algorithm) into an MoE model: 32 experts and 456B TOTAL parameters, of which 45.9B are ACTIVATED per token (about 10.1 percent active). Two supporting systems contributions are what made the scale reachable: an optimised parallel strategy and highly efficient computation-communication OVERLAP techniques for MoE dispatch and for lightning attention itself, so the all-to-all and the attention kernel are hidden behind other work. Because lightning attention holds a fixed-size state, the long-context claim (4M tokens for MiniMax-Text-01) does not come with a proportionally growing KV cache, which is the entire serving argument for the architecture at this scale.
notes: arXiv preprint; no journal-ref. The 45.9B-active-of-456B-total figure is quoted directly from the abstract and is the number to carry into serving capacity planning. speedup_reported is null: the paper claims efficient training and inference on hundreds-of-billions scale and superior long-context capability versus other models, but states no tok/s ratio with baseline and settings. Engine support verified in llama.cpp: LLM_ARCH_MINIMAX_01, LLM_ARCH_MINIMAX_M2 and LLM_ARCH_MINIMAX_M3 exist, MINIMAX_01 is classified hybrid by llm_arch_is_hybrid(), and conversion/minimax.py is present. Successor MiniMax-M1 is recorded separately.
